feedback.problem:
Compute the variance ${\sigma }^{2}$ of a data set ${x}_{i}$ consisting of $12$ data points, where 

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{12}{x}_{i}=-60,\,{\sum }_{i=1}^{12}{x}_{i}^{2}=440.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
If we have a data set that consists of the points ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n},$ then the variance can be computed as

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2},
$$

where $\overset{―}{x}$ is the mean of the data set and $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}$ is the mean of the squares of the points in the data set.

First, let's compute $\overset{―}{x}.$ There are $n=12$ points in our data set, and we know that ${\sum }_{i=1}^{12}{x}_{i}=-60,$ so we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{12}{\sum }_{i=1}^{12}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{12}\cdot (-60) \\  & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's compute $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}.$ We know that ${\sum }_{i=1}^{12}{x}_{i}^{2}=440,$ so we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{12}{\sum }_{i=1}^{12}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{12}\cdot 440 \\  & =\frac{440}{12} \\  & =\frac{110}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =\frac{110}{3}-{(-5)}^{2} \\  & =\frac{110}{3}-25 \\  & =\frac{110-75}{3} \\  & =\frac{35}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
